violations.why: The measure ISR reads numberOfRecords as the index, then the communicate ISR resets it. The measure ISR then increments a stale value and overwrites the reset.
The index read at line 83 and the read in the increment at line 85 can see different values if the higher-priority ISR resets the counter between them.
After the measure ISR increments tickCounter, the communicate ISR can overwrite it. The measure ISR then reads a value it didn't write.
The measure ISR reads tickCounter and later writes 0 to it. A reset by the communicate ISR in between is overwritten.
The non-atomic increment of intervalCounter can be preempted by the communicate ISR's reset. The measure ISR then writes back a stale value and loses the reset.
